Privacy Act of 1974 This act ensures consumer privacy and control over personal information. The continued presence of a charged-off account beyond its permissible reporting period raises privacy concerns. 
Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( 15 USC 1692 ) The FDCPA prohibits unfair or deceptive practices in debt collection. The ongoing report of a charged-off debt may suggest improper debt collection practices. 
IRS Regulations on Discharged Debt According to IRS rules, a discharged or forgiven debt should not be reported on a credit report. Additionally, the absence of a 1099-C form, which confirms a discharged debt for tax purposes, raises questions about the accuracy of this charge-off.

Investigation into Compliance with IRS Regulations Examine whether XXXX  XXXX issued a 1099-C, as required by IRS regulations XXXX for this charged-off debt. 
Review of Account Handling Investigate whether XXXX  XXXX violated any provisions of the Fair Credit Reporting Act, Fair Credit Billing Act, or Fair Debt Collection Practices Act. 
I request a prompt response and appropriate action to correct this situation. If further information or documentation is required, I am prepared to provide it upon request. Thank you for your attention to this matter, and I look forward to hearing from you soon.

As per the Fair Credit Reporting Act, a consumer report is defined as follows : " The term 'consumer report ' means any written, oral, or other communication of any information by a consumer reporting agency bearing on a consumers creditworthiness, credit standing, credit capacity, character, general reputation, personal characteristics, or mode of living which is used or expected to be used or collected in whole or in part for the purpose of serving as a factor in establishing the consumers eligibility for ( A ) credit or insurance to be used primarily for personal, family, or household purposes ; ( B ) employment purposes ; or ( C ) any other purpose authorized under section 1681b of this title. '' The exclusion section, or 15 USC 1681a ( 2 ) A ( i ), explicitly states : " The term 'consumer report ' does not include ( A ) subject to section 1681s3 of this title, any ( i ) report containing information solely as to transactions or experiences between the consumer and the person making the report. Failure to comply with the above requests will result in legal action against your agency, with the possibility of significant monetary compensation. This notice will be submitted to the Federal Trade Commission and Consumer Financial Protection Bureau.

Should this matter remain unresolved, your agency will be implicated in criminal violations with consumer reporting agencies, and your CEO or a high-ranking official will be held liable for criminal penalties pursuant to 18 USC 894 .

( a ) Duty of furnishers of information to provide accurate information ( 1 ) Prohibition ( A ) Reporting information with actual knowledge of errors A person shall not furnish any information relating to a consumer to any consumer reporting agency if the person knows or has reasonable cause to believe that the information is inaccurate. ( B ) Reporting information after notice and confirmation of errors A person shall not furnish information relating to a consumer to any consumer reporting agency if ( i ) the person has been notified by the consumer, at the address specified by the person for such notices, that specific information is inaccurate; and ( ii ) the information is, in fact, inaccurate. Also, 15 U.S. Code 6801 - Protection of nonpublic personal information. It is the policy of the Congress that each financial institution has an affirmative and continuing obligation to respect the privacy of its customers and to protect the security and confidentiality of those customers ' nonpublic personal information.

The issues I have experienced relate to predatory lending practices, failure to disclose substantial fees, and the refusal to provide a decline letter, which has caused me significant financial loss. 

I applied for a loan with Guaranteed Rate Affinity after being declined by XXXX  XXXX XXXX and XXXX. I was approved for a mortgage with an initial loan estimate of approximately {$88000.00}. However, just two days before closing, I was presented with a final loan estimate that was more than {$10000.00} higher than the initial estimate. This increase was unexpected, and I did not have sufficient funds to cover the additional amount. Upon consulting with my attorney, we realized that additional fees, including legal fees, had not been disclosed, further exacerbating the issue. 

I informed Guaranteed Rate Affinity of my financial situation and my inability to proceed. However, instead of declining my loan due to insufficient funds ( which would have allowed me to terminate my contract with the condo seller without penalty ), they pressured me to voluntarily withdraw my loan application. I believe this practice is unfair and caused me to forfeit 50 % of my down payment, as I was unable to secure the decline letter, which was a stipulation in the contract with the seller. 

I never contacted Guaranteed Rate Affinity to voluntarily withdraw from the loan application, and I would like to know what reasoning they had in asking me to withdraw, rather than reaching out to my lawyer, who should have handled such a critical decision. I feel it is predatory to pressure a borrower into withdrawing from a loan application without allowing proper time for consultation, and I believe Guaranteed Rate Affinity was well aware of the potential harm this could cause. 

Additionally, I find it concerning that, despite the closing being set for XX/XX/XXXX, I received a call on XX/XX/XXXX from XXXX XXXX, asking if I would like to withdraw my loan application. This call was made while my attorney was on vacation, and no efforts were made to explore all possible options. I question the timing and motives behind this call and the pressure placed on me to withdraw without representation. 

Moreover, I believe Guaranteed Rate Affinity engaged in predatory lending practices by suggesting that I find additional funds or sell assets to complete the purchase. I was led into a financially precarious situation without being fully informed of all the fees and potential liabilities, which I believe violates consumer protection laws. 

I am requesting the following actions : An investigation into the lending practices of Guaranteed Rate Affinity related to my mortgage application. 
A determination of whether Guaranteed Rate Affinitys failure to provide a decline letter and their pressure for me to withdraw my application constitutes a violation of federal lending laws. 
Compensation for the financial losses I have incurred due to these actions, including the loss of 50 % of my down payment and any associated legal fees. 

I have attached documentation related to my mortgage application, loan estimates, and communications with Guaranteed Rate Affinity. Please feel free to contact me for any additional information or clarification. 

Thank you for your attention to this matter. I look forward to your prompt investigation and resolution of my complaint. 

Sincerely, XXXX XXXX

XX/XX/year> To Whom It May Concern : I, XXXX XXXX, am submitting a formal complaint against Navient, a student loan servicer, for their failure to provide adequate service and for engaging in practices that have caused significant financial harm to me as a borrower. Below are the specific details of my complaint : 1. Misleading and Confusing Information Regarding Repayment Options Navient has consistently provided me with incorrect, incomplete, or misleading information regarding my repayment options. When I initially sought guidance on available repayment plans, particularly income-driven repayment ( IDR ) plans, I was not informed of all available options. Navient representatives provided incomplete details, failing to explain key aspects of these plans, including eligibility criteria, payment calculations, and how to apply for forgiveness programs under these plans. 

In addition, when I requested information on consolidating my loans and entering a new repayment plan, the guidance I received was both inconsistent and contradictory, causing further confusion. As a result, I was unable to make informed decisions, leading to missed opportunities to lower my monthly payments and ultimately increasing my total loan burden.

2. Failure to Properly Apply Payments Over the course of several months, I have experienced numerous instances where Navient failed to properly apply payments to my account. Despite submitting timely payments, these payments were either applied to the wrong loan or not credited to my account at all, causing my account to reflect inaccurate balances. I was subsequently charged late fees and accrued additional interest due to Navient 's misapplication of my payments. 

Despite multiple calls to their customer service department to resolve these issues, the problem persists, and I have not been given a clear explanation for why payments are not being applied correctly. This has caused severe financial distress, as I am now facing a higher loan balance and additional fees that should not have been assessed.

3. Failure to Provide Accurate Information on Loan Forgiveness Programs I am also extremely dissatisfied with Navient 's handling of loan forgiveness programs. I have contacted Navient on numerous occasions to inquire about my eligibility for Public Service Loan Forgiveness ( PSLF ) and other forgiveness options, as I have been working in a qualifying public service position for several years. However, Navient failed to provide accurate information regarding the specific requirements of the PSLF program and did not properly track my qualifying payments toward forgiveness.

As a result of this failure, I am not receiving credit for all the payments I have made while employed in a public service position. This has caused significant delays in my progress toward loan forgiveness, unfairly extending the time I must continue making payments on my loans.

4. Steering Into Forbearance Instead of Income-Driven Repayment Plans When I reached out to Navient to discuss options for lowering my payments during periods of financial hardship, I was steered into forbearance instead of being properly informed about income-driven repayment plans, which would have been a better solution for my financial situation. As a result, my loan balance increased due to the accumulation of interest during the periods of forbearance, which was not clearly explained to me at the time. This has further increased my financial burden and delayed my progress toward eventual loan forgiveness.

5. Poor Customer Service and Lack of Accountability The level of customer service provided by Navient has been consistently poor. Representatives frequently provide conflicting information, fail to follow up on issues, and seem ill-equipped to handle even basic inquiries about loan repayment and servicing. I have been forced to spend hours on the phone trying to resolve issues that should have been addressed promptly, and my requests for escalation to higher levels of management have often been ignored or dismissed.

In addition to these systemic issues, Navient has shown a lack of accountability when addressing the errors they have caused in my account. I have not received satisfactory explanations or resolutions for the misapplied payments, inaccurate balance calculations, and improper guidance regarding repayment options and loan forgiveness.

Conclusion and Desired Resolution Navient 's actionsor lack thereofhave caused significant financial harm and emotional distress. As a student loan borrower, I relied on Navient to provide accurate and timely information about my loans and repayment options, yet they have consistently failed to do so. I am seeking the following resolutions : 1. A thorough review of my loan account to ensure that all payments are properly applied and credited, with any incorrect charges, late fees, or accrued interest removed from my account.

2. An accurate reassessment of my eligibility and progress toward Public Service Loan Forgiveness ( PSLF ) and other loan forgiveness programs, with appropriate credit given for all qualifying payments made to date.

3. Reimbursement for any fees and interest accrued as a result of Navient 's failure to provide accurate information about income-driven repayment plans and their improper steering into forbearance.

4. A formal explanation from Navient acknowledging their errors and detailing corrective actions taken to prevent these issues from recurring.

5. Compensation for the financial harm and emotional distress caused by Navient 's failure to provide competent and reliable service.

I trust that the CFPB will take my complaint seriously and investigate Navient 's practices thoroughly. Navient 's behavior has not only impacted my financial well-being but has also caused widespread harm to countless other borrowers who rely on them for accurate loan servicing.

Thank you for your time and attention to this matter. I look forward to a resolution that addresses the issues outlined above and prevents further harm to other borrowers. 

Sincerely, XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX

Consumer complaint narrative:
I am writing to formally lodge a complaint against Affirm regarding the mishandling of refunds and improper loan management. 

On two separate occasions, I purchased headlights from XXXX, both of which were returned due to issues with the products. The first purchase was made on XX/XX/XXXX and totaled {$560.00}, for which I made an initial payment of {$57.00}, and a loan was initiated through Affirm. Upon receiving the headlights, I found that they were not as described, so I returned them and used a second loan through Affirm to purchase a different set of headlights on XX/XX/XXXX, this time totaling {$1000.00}. This resulted in two open loans with Affirm, which should have been resolved once my refunds were processed. 

XXXX issued the refund for the first purchase of {$560.00} on XX/XX/XXXX, and I received confirmation from both XXXX and Affirm. However, Affirms email indicated that if I did not select which loan to apply the refund to, it would automatically be applied to the loan with the highest interest rate. When I followed the link in the email to choose the appropriate loan, I was repeatedly met with an error page stating : Oops! We can't find the page you're looking for. Did you want to view your loans or get a virtual card? You can also see our FAQ for help. 

I attempted to resolve this using multiple browsers and devices, but the same error occurred each time. Assuming the email was sent in error, I waited for the refund to be applied. However, when the refund was processed, it was applied to the larger, second loan, leaving me with two active loans. I contacted Affirm and requested that the refund be applied to the correct loan. I was informed that once a refund was applied, it could not be reversed and that I should have called in if I encountered issues with the email link. Frustrated, I chose to pay off the remaining balance on the larger loan ( {$1000.00} ) to avoid paying interest on two loans simultaneously. 

Shortly after, I was informed by my technician that the second set of headlights ( which cost {$1000.00} ) was defective. I initiated a return with XXXX and received confirmation of the refund on XX/XX/XXXX. Again, Affirm sent an email with the same instructions, and once more, I encountered the same error message when attempting to follow the link. This time, I called Affirm directly. The representative I spoke to was unhelpful and seemed confused by the issue. After a second attempt, I spoke with another representative who acknowledged that something was wrong and escalated my case to a different department. 

Since then, I have been given the runaround by Affirm. Despite multiple follow-ups, I have not received any communication from the department handling my case. On XX/XX/XXXX, I received my second refund from XXXX, but Affirm has still not applied the refund correctly. As a result, I have not received any funds for the proper amount of the refund and I am still being charged for an open loan that should have been closed as of XX/XX/XXXX, had Affirm applied the refund correctly or if the email link functioned properly. 

I am now missing a substantial amount of money that should have been refunded to me, and I continue to make payments on a loan that should no longer exist. I respectfully request that this matter be investigated and resolved promptly.

This complaint specifically addresses Rubin & Rothman, LLCs ( the collector ) attempts to collect on a debt purportedly owed to XXXX XXXX, and XXXX alleged issuance of a 1099-C form to the IRS without notifying me. 

1. Failure to Provide 1099-C Notification : XXXX XXXX . appears to have filed a 1099-C form with the IRS in relation to this debt. Due to XXXX apparent filing of a 1099-C, Rubin & Rothman , LLC may be reporting a debt that has been discharged or forgiven, leading to a potentially inaccurate credit report entry. 
Failure to Provide Debt Validation : Under the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ), 15 U.S.C. 1692g ( b ), I am entitled to a validation of the debt. However, despite my request, Rubin & Rothman , LLC has failed to provide me with a debt validation letter, creating further uncertainty about the legitimacy of this debt.

This filing is a violation of the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ), 15 U.S.C. 1692i, which requires debt collectors to bring legal action either in the district where the consumer resides or where the contract was signed. Since I do not reside in New York and did not sign the contract in New York, this lawsuit constitutes an improper venue and is thus unlawful.

The card recommended by Credit Karma was another XXXX card. I clicked the referral link Credit Karma provided and went through the application process at chase.com. 

During the application process at chase.com, XXXX requested the account number of the card I intended to to transfer the balance from, as well as the amount I wanted to transfer. 

I entered the account number of the XXXX XXXX XXXX card, as well as the amount ( {$5000.00} ). 

I entered that information, clicked " continue '' and was then notified that my application was accepted and I was enrolled in a new card with a credit limit of {$1500.00} ( I was expecting {$5000.00} and there was no " confirm '' button to accept enrollment with this credit limit - it simply enrolled me immediately ). 

After I was enrolled in the card, I reached out to XXXX about this, and they informed me that my balance transfer was ineligible, as XXXX does not allow the transfer of balances between cards that they administer. As the original card was a XXXX XXXX XXXX card, and my new card was a XXXX card, the new card was essentially useless to me. Furthermore, there would be hard-pulls on my credit profiles that would not be rescinded. Neither XXXX nor Credit Karma agreed to provided supplemental documentation for my appeal to the credit bureaus. 

I asked for more information, and XXXX indicated that this policy is quite common across lending institution- to prohibit customers from openeing new cards at the same bank and transferring balances between them. 

When I mentioned that the application process included inputting the original high-interest card account number ( XXXX XXXX XXXX card ) and a balance transfer amount, and the application under the auspices of a balance transfer was accepted, despite XXXX explicitly requesting the information that it should have used to inform the consumer of balance transfer ineligibility, XXXX indicated that the policy regarding balance transfers is in their terms and conditions. ( i ) National security freeze ( 1 ) Definitions For purposes of this subsection : ( A ) The term consumer reporting agency means a consumer reporting agency described in section 1681a ( p ) of this title.

( B ) The term proper identification has the meaning of such term as used under section 1681h of this title.

( C ) The term security freeze means a restriction that prohibits a consumer reporting agency from disclosing the contents of a consumer report that is subject to such security freeze to any person requesting the consumer report.

( 2 ) Placement of security freeze ( A ) In general Upon receiving a direct request from a consumer that a consumer reporting agency place a security freeze, and upon receiving proper identification from the consumer, the consumer reporting agency shall, free of charge, place the security freeze not later than ( i ) in the case of a request that is by toll-free telephone or secure electronic means, 1 business day after receiving the request directly from the consumer; or ( ii ) in the case of a request that is by mail, 3 business days after receiving the request directly from the consumer.

( B ) Confirmation and additional information Not later than 5 business days after placing a security freeze under subparagraph ( A ), a consumer reporting agency shall ( i ) send confirmation of the placement to the consumer ; and ( ii ) inform the consumer of ( I ) the process by which the consumer may remove the security freeze, including a mechanism to authenticate the consumer ; and ( II ) the consumers right described in section 1681m ( d ) ( 1 ) ( D ) of this title.

( C ) Notice to third parties A consumer reporting agency may advise a third party that a security freeze has been placed with respect to a consumer under subparagraph ( A ).

( 3 ) Removal of security freeze ( A ) In general A consumer reporting agency shall remove a security freeze placed on the consumer report of a consumer only in the following cases : ( i ) Upon the direct request of the consumer.

( ii ) The security freeze was placed due to a material misrepresentation of fact by the consumer.

( B ) Notice if removal not by request If a consumer reporting agency removes a security freeze under subparagraph ( A ) ( ii ), the consumer reporting agency shall notify the consumer in writing prior to removing the security freeze.

( C ) Removal of security freeze by consumer request Except as provided in subparagraph ( A ) ( ii ), a security freeze shall remain in place until the consumer directly requests that the security freeze be removed. Upon receiving a direct request from a consumer that a consumer reporting agency remove a security freeze, and upon receiving proper identification from the consumer, the consumer reporting agency shall, free of charge, remove the security freeze not later than ( i ) in the case of a request that is by toll-free telephone or secure electronic means, 1 hour after receiving the request for removal ; or ( ii ) in the case of a request that is by mail, 3 business days after receiving the request for removal.

( D ) Third-party requests If a third party requests access to a consumer report of a consumer with respect to which a security freeze is in effect, where such request is in connection with an application for credit, and the consumer does not allow such consumer report to be accessed, the third party may treat the application as incomplete.

( E ) Temporary removal of security freeze Upon receiving a direct request from a consumer under subparagraph ( A ) ( i ), if the consumer requests a temporary removal of a security freeze, the consumer reporting agency shall, in accordance with subparagraph ( C ), remove the security freeze for the period of time specified by the consumer.

( 4 ) Exceptions A security freeze shall not apply to the making of a consumer report for use of the following : ( A ) A person or entity, or a subsidiary, affiliate, or agent of that person or entity, or an assignee of a financial obligation owed by the consumer to that person or entity, or a prospective assignee of a financial obligation owed by the consumer to that person or entity in conjunction with the proposed purchase of the financial obligation, with which the consumer has or had prior to assignment an account or contract including a demand deposit account, or to whom the consumer issued a negotiable instrument, for the purposes of reviewing the account or collecting the financial obligation owed for the account, contract, or negotiable instrument. For purposes of this subparagraph, reviewing the account includes activities related to account maintenance, monitoring, credit line increases, and account upgrades and enhancements.

( B ) Any Federal, State, or local agency, law enforcement agency, trial court, or private collection agency acting pursuant to a court order, warrant, or subpoena.

( C ) A child support agency acting pursuant to part D of title IV of the Social Security Act ( 42 U.S.C. 651 et seq. ).

( D ) A Federal agency or a State or its agents or assigns acting to investigate fraud or acting to investigate or collect delinquent taxes or unpaid court orders or to fulfill any of its other statutory responsibilities, provided such responsibilities are consistent with a permissible purpose under section 1681b of this title.

( E ) By a person using credit information for the purposes described under section 1681b ( c ) of this title.

( F ) Any person or entity administering a credit file monitoring subscription or similar service to which the consumer has subscribed.

( G ) Any person or entity for the purpose of providing a consumer with a copy of the consumers consumer report or credit score, upon the request of the consumer.

( H ) Any person using the information in connection with the underwriting of insurance.

( I ) Any person using the information for employment, tenant, or background screening purposes.

( J ) Any person using the information for assessing, verifying, or authenticating a consumers identity for purposes other than the granting of credit, or for investigating or preventing actual or potential fraud.

( 5 ) Notice of rights At any time a consumer is required to receive a summary of rights required under section 1681g of this title, the following notice shall be included : Consumers Have the Right To Obtain a Security Freeze You have a right to place a security freeze on your credit report, which will prohibit a consumer reporting agency from releasing information in your credit report without your express authorization. The security freeze is designed to prevent credit, loans, and services from being approved in your name without your consent. However, you should be aware that using a security freeze to take control over who gets access to the personal and financial information in your credit report may delay, interfere with, or prohibit the timely approval of any subsequent request or application you make regarding a new loan, credit, mortgage, or any other account involving the extension of credit.

As an alternative to a security freeze, you have the right to place an initial or extended fraud alert on your credit file at no cost. An initial fraud alert is a 1-year alert that is placed on a consumers credit file. Upon seeing a fraud alert display on a consumers credit file, a business is required to take steps to verify the consumers identity before extending new credit. If you are a victim of identity theft, you are entitled to an extended fraud alert, which is a fraud alert lasting 7 years.

A security freeze does not apply to a person or entity, or its affiliates, or collection agencies acting on behalf of the person or entity, with which you have an existing account that requests information in your credit report for the purposes of reviewing or collecting the account. Reviewing the account includes activities related to account maintenance, monitoring, credit line increases, and account upgrades and enhancements..

( 6 ) Webpage ( A ) Consumer reporting agencies A consumer reporting agency shall establish a webpage that ( i ) allows a consumer to request a security freeze ; ( ii ) allows a consumer to request an initial fraud alert ; ( iii ) allows a consumer to request an extended fraud alert ; ( iv ) allows a consumer to request an XXXX XXXX fraud alert ; ( v ) allows a consumer to opt-out of the use of information in a consumer report to send the consumer a solicitation of credit or insurance, in accordance with section 1681m ( d ) of this title; and ( vi ) shall not be the only mechanism by which a consumer may request a security freeze.

( j ) National protection for files and credit records of protected consumers ( 1 ) Definitions As used in this subsection : ( A ) The term consumer reporting agency means a consumer reporting agency described in section 1681a ( p ) of this title.

Dear Consumer, XXXX XXXX XXXX, I am writing to formally dispute inaccurate information on my credit report maintained by Transunion, XXXX, and XXXX. The late payment reported on my credit report falls under the category of information solely as to transactions or experiences between the consumer and the person making the report. As such, it should not be considered a consumer report and should be removed from my credit file.

I believe that this inaccurate information is in violation of the FCRA and is causing me significant harm. I request that the CFPB take immediate action to address this issue and ensure that my credit report is corrected.

Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter. I look forward to your response.

To whom this may concern, On XX/XX/XXXX, at XXXX XXXX., I called the Equifax fraud department regarding two unauthorized inquiries appearing on my consumer report. The department acknowledged the inquiries and instructed me to file a detailed dispute report with the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau ( CFPB ) to address the unauthorized activity. Accordingly, I hereby provide notice of the two inquiries, which were made without a permissible purpose, and demand their prompt removal from my credit report. 
The Federal Fair Credit Reporting Act, explicitly states that a credit reporting agency is prohibited from furnishing unauthorized inquiries on a consumer 's report without proper authorization. I kindly request that you take immediate action to rectify this issue by removing the unauthorized inquiry listed below from my consumer report. Your prompt attention to this matter is greatly appreciated. 

The Unaturized Inquiries are, " XXXX XXXX '' on XX/XX/XXXX and " XXXX XXXX '' on XX/XX/XXXX, I trust that you will handle this matter with the utmost urgency and ensure that my consumer report is accurately reflected in accordance with the Federal Fair Credit Reporting Act. According to the Federal Legislative Fair Credit Reporting Act 15 U.S.C 1681b ( 2a ) - Permissible purposes of consumer reports. A Disclosure to the consumer means, ( A ) In general Except as provided in subparagraph ( B ), a person may not procure a consumer report, or cause a consumer report to be procured, for employment purposes with respect to any consumer, unless ( i ) A clear and conspicuous disclosure has been made in writing to the consumer at any time before the report is procured or caused to be procured, in a document that consists solely of the disclosure, that a consumer report may be obtained for employment purposes ; and ( ii ) the consumer has authorized in writing ( which authorization may be made on the document referred to in clause ( i ) ) the procurement of the report by that person. Now that we have established notice that these inquiries are fraudulent, I need these inquiries blocked and deleted as per, 15 U.S. Code 1681g - Disclosures to consumers : Every consumer reporting agency shall, upon request, and subject to section 1681h ( a ) ( 1 ) of this title, clearly and accurately disclose to the consumer : ( 5 ) A record of all inquiries received by the agency during the 1-year period preceding the request that identified the consumer in connection with a credit or insurance transaction that was not initiated by the consumer. As per 15 U.S. Code 1681s2, it is clearly stated that credit reporting agencies have a duty to investigate and correct any inaccurate or incomplete information on a consumer 's credit report. Failure to investigate and correct inaccurate or incomplete information on a consumer 's credit report may result in legal action. Once again thank you for your immediate attention to this matter. As per 15 U.S. Code 1681s2, A person shall not furnish information relating to a consumer to any consumer reporting agency if ( i ) the person has been notified by the consumer, at the address specified by the person for such notices, that specific information is inaccurate; and ( ii ) the information is, in fact, inaccurate. Following the necessary updates made to my consumer report, I kindly request that you provide me with an updated report reflecting these changes. It is imperative that the report accurately reflects my current credit information. I am not requesting for Validation or Verification. Furthermore, I must emphasize that you are now aware of the importance I place on the proper handling of my consumer report in accordance with the Fair Credit Reporting Act. I trust that you will fulfill your obligations under the law and ensure the accuracy and integrity of my credit information. Thank you for your attention to this matter.

COMPLAINT FOR VIOLATION OF THE FAIR CREDIT REPORTING ACT INTRODUCTION This is an action for damages brought by Plaintiff XXXX XXXX, an individual, against Defendant Toyota Motor Credit Corporation ( Toyota ), for violations of the Fair Credit Reporting Act, 15 U.S.C. 1681 et seq. ( " FCRA '' ). 
Defendant Toyota failed to conduct a reasonable investigation into Plaintiffs dispute regarding its erroneous reporting of her account status, in violation of 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( b ). 
JURISDICTION AND VENUE This Court has jurisdiction under 15 U.S.C. 1681p and 28 U.S.C. 1331, as this action arises under federal law. 
Venue is proper in this District under 28 U.S.C. 1391 ( b ) because Toyota Motor Credit Corporation is subject to personal jurisdiction in this District and a substantial part of the events giving rise to the claim occurred here. 
PARTIES Plaintiff XXXX XXXX is a consumer as defined by the FCRA, 15 U.S.C. 1681a ( c ), residing at XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX, NY XXXX. 
Defendant Toyota Motor Credit Corporation is a furnisher of credit information, with its principal address at : Toyota Motor Credit Corporation XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, GA XXXXToyota regularly furnishes credit information to consumer reporting agencies such as XXXX, XXXX, and XXXX . 
FACTUAL ALLEGATIONS Plaintiff obtained her credit report from the three major consumer reporting agencies ( XXXX, XXXX, and XXXX ) and discovered inaccuracies related to her Toyota Motor Credit Corporation account ( Account Number : XXXX ). 
Specifically, Defendant Toyota inaccurately reported the date of last payment on Plaintiffs account inconsistently, with XXXX and XXXX reporting XX/XX/year>, while XXXX reported XX/XX/year>. 
Toyota also inaccurately reported the payment history, indicating a 60-day late status on all three credit reports as of XX/XX/year>, without sufficient investigation into the accuracy of such information. 
Plaintiff disputed the inaccurate information with the consumer reporting agencies and requested that Toyota conduct a reasonable investigation into her claim. 
Upon information and belief, Toyota failed to conduct a reasonable investigation, instead relying solely on its internal records without evaluating Plaintiffs account history or verifying the accuracy of the reported information. 
Defendants actions caused Plaintiffs credit score to decline, affecting her creditworthiness and resulting in economic and reputational harm. 
COUNT I VIOLATION OF THE FAIR CREDIT REPORTING ACT ( 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( b ) ) Plaintiff re-alleges and incorporates by reference each of the above paragraphs as though fully set forth herein. 
Under 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( b ), after receiving notice of a dispute from a consumer reporting agency, a furnisher is required to conduct a reasonable investigation to verify the accuracy of the disputed information. 
Toyota Motor Credit Corporation received notice of Plaintiffs dispute from the consumer reporting agencies regarding the inconsistencies in payment history and last payment date. 
Toyota willfully and/or negligently failed to conduct a reasonable investigation of the disputed information and instead verified inaccurate information to consumer reporting agencies without taking any corrective action. 
Defendant 's inadequate investigation has caused Plaintiff to suffer harm, including but not limited to, lowered credit scores, denials of credit, and other damages. 
PRAYER FOR RELIEF WHEREFORE, Plaintiff XXXX XXXX requests that judgment be entered in her favor and against Defendant Toyota Motor Credit Corporation for the following relief : a. Actual damages in an amount to be determined at trial ; b. Statutory damages for each violation of the FCRA ; c. Punitive damages as allowed under the FCRA ; d. Attorneys fees and costs as provided by 15 U.S.C. 1681n and 15 U.S.C. 1681o ; e. Such other relief as this Court deems just and proper.

I was informed on that call that Experian did not conduct any investigation of the account and simply asked the creditor entity on file, XXXX XXXX XXXXXX/XX/XXXX to confirm the account information, which they apparently did without further detail or explanation. The Experian representative I spoke to at this time told me that if I wanted Experian to actually do any reasonable investigation of its own, I would have to submit a second dispute specifically requesting that Experian do some form of investigation of even basic information about the account ( such as the dollar amount alleged to be owed, how/when/where it was accumulated, and why they think I am responsible for paying it ). Which brings us to today, XX/XX/year>. I was informed today by Experian 's automated system that once again my dispute request had been completed, and that there were no changes to the account. Exasperated and demoralized by Experian 's sham " dispute '' process, I have given up on my fruitless attempts at getting Experian to - as clearly required by the FCRA - conduct a reasonable and actual investigation into this disputed collection account. As such, I am asking that the CFPB involve itself in making Experian conduct a proper investigation into my dispute as the FCRA in no uncertain terms requires. It has come to my attention that certain accounts listed on my credit report do not belong to me, and their inclusion is not only inaccurate but also violates my rights as a consumer. Allow me to elaborate on the specific issues I have identified and the laws that support my claim : **15 U.S Code 1681a ( 4 ) - Consumer Right to Privacy : ** The presence of fraudulent accounts on my credit report constitutes an intrusion into my privacy rights. I firmly believe that I have the sole authority to determine what information is private and should be shared on my credit report.

**FDCPA 807 - Misleading False Reporting : ** The information being reported falsely suggests that I have applied for numerous inquiries and accounts, which is simply not the case. This misleading representation can have detrimental effects on my financial standing and is a violation of the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ).

**15 USC 1681n - Civil Liability for Willful Noncompliance : ** Your agency 's failure to verify the accuracy of credit information before reporting it may result in civil liability. It is imperative that accurate and verified information is reported to ensure fairness and transparency in the credit reporting process.

**18 U.S. Code 1028A - Aggravated Identity Theft : ** Sharing my personal information with creditors without obtaining my consent may constitute aggravated identity theft, a serious criminal offense punishable by law.

**15 U.S. Code 6802 ( b ) 1 ( ) ( a ) ( A ) ( B ) ( C ) - Obligations with Respect to Disclosures of Personal Information : ** Your agency 's failure to disclose my right to opt out of information sharing is concerning and deceptive. As a consumer, I should have the option to exercise my right to privacy and confidentiality regarding my personal information.

**FDCPA 8012 - Furnishing Deceptive Forms : ** Reporting unvalidated debts without proper verification is misleading and deceptive. It is essential that accurate and verified information is reported to avoid any misrepresentation of my financial status.

**15 U.S. Code 1692f - Unfair Practices : ** Reporting unvalidated debts as if they were accurate constitutes an unfair practice. It is essential that all reported information is verified and validated to ensure fairness and accuracy.

**15 U.S. Code 1602 - Definitions and Rules of Construction : ** As the original creditor, I did not grant authorization for the deferral of payments. Your agency 's reporting of inaccurate information violates my rights and undermines the integrity of the credit reporting process.

**FDCPA 806 - Harassment and Abuse : ** Your agency 's actions have caused me undue distress and inconvenience. Despite my efforts to rectify the situation, inaccurate information continues to be reported without my consent, leading to ongoing harassment from creditors.

**Section 1581a ( 3 ) - Identity Theft : ** The illegal acquisition of my personal information and its unauthorized use by creditors constitutes identity theft, a serious offense that must be addressed.

**15 U.S. Code 1692b ( 2 ) - Acquisition of Location Information : ** Reporting debts without my consent is a clear violation of my rights and further compounds the inaccuracies present in my credit report. 

**15 U.S. Code 1666b - Timing of Payments : ** Reporting " late payments '' without a clear definition is both inaccurate and deceptive. It is crucial that accurate information is reported to ensure fairness and transparency in the credit reporting process.

**15 U.S. Code 1605 - Determination of Finance Charge : ** Inclusion of inaccurate finance charges further exacerbates the inaccuracies present in my credit report and must be rectified immediately.

**15 U.S. Code 1692d ( 1 ) - Harassment and Abuse : ** Reporting unvalidated debts negatively impacts my reputation and constitutes harassment and abuse. It is imperative that all reported information is accurate and verified to avoid any misrepresentation of my financial status.

**15 U.S. Code 1692j - Furnishing Certain Deceptive Forms : ** Any contracts signed without my authorization constitute a violation of this statute and must be addressed accordingly.

**15 USC 1692h - Multiple Debts : ** Any payments made on unvalidated debts must be returned to me promptly, as per this statute. 

**15 U.S. Code 1692g - Validation of Debts : ** Only I can validate debts, and your agency 's failure to remove unvalidated accounts is a violation of my rights as a consumer.

**15 U.S. Code 1681b - Permissible Purposes of Consumer Reports : ** Reporting information without obtaining written consent violates this statute and undermines the integrity of the credit reporting process.

**15 USC 1681i Procedure in case of disputed accuracy : ** Under this law, when a consumer notifies a furnisher that they believe there is inaccurate information on their credit report, the furnisher is required to conduct a reasonable investigation into the dispute. This investigation typically involves reviewing the relevant information provided by the consumer, as well as any supporting documentation, and then either verifying, correcting, or deleting the disputed information as necessary. 

The furnisher must complete the investigation within a reasonable timeframe, generally within 30 days, although extensions may be granted under certain circumstances. Once the investigation is complete, the furnisher must report the results back to the consumer and, if applicable, update the information with the CRAs.

Failure to comply with the requirements of **15 U.S. Code 1681i** can result in penalties for the furnisher, including fines and potential legal action by the consumer.

Overall, this law ensures that consumers have the right to challenge and correct inaccurate information on their credit reports, helping to maintain the integrity and fairness of the credit reporting system.

The law requires companies to delete disputed unverified information from consumer reports. 

Credit reports are used to make decisions that affect every facet of peoples lives. Credit reports compiled by consumer reporting companies are used by lenders, insurers, employers, landlords, and othersyet these reports frequently contain errors. By one estimate, one in five Americans has an error on at least one credit report. Accordingly, it is critical that people have a meaningful opportunity to correct inaccuracies on their reports. Thats why Congresswhen it passed the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ) required credit reporting companies, and the companies that give them information, to respond appropriately when notified of errors. 

As the federal government agency charged with implementing and administering the federal consumer financial laws, the CFPB is committed to ensuring that companies meet the obligations put on them by Congress in the law. For that reason, yesterday the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau ( CFPB ) and the Federal Trade Commission ( FTC ), which both enforce fair credit reporting laws, filed an amicus brief in the U.S. Court of Appeals for XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX  to help ensure that companies that provide information to credit reporting companies comply with the law. Specifically, they must tell credit reporting companies to remove information that they can not verify after someone identifies the information as wrong. 

Companies responsibility to remove unverified information The FCRA provides people multiple ways to dispute inaccurate information on their credit reports. Commonly, people dispute the accuracy of information on their credit reports with a credit reporting company, such as XXXX, XXXX, or XXXX. In response, the credit reporting company often refers the dispute to the company that provided the disputed information. Failure to Provide Proper Validation of Debt Under the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ), 15 U.S.C. 1692g ( b ), a debt collector is required to provide proper validation of the debt upon request. The itemized bill you provided is insufficient to verify that I am the owner of this debt. Therefore, I am formally requesting a copy of the original signed agreement, along with any forms of identification ( e.g., drivers license, Social Security number ) provided to the original creditor. 2. Failure to Notify of Charge-Off If this debt was charged off by the original creditor, I was not properly informed as required by law. The Truth in Lending Act ( TILA ), 15 U.S.C. 1666a, stipulates that creditors must notify consumers of charge-offs before reporting them to credit reporting agencies. The Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ), 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( a ), further enforces that creditors must accurately report information to credit bureaus. If the original creditor failed to inform me of the charge-off, both the TILA and the FCRA have been violated. 
3. Failure to Send Validation Notice to Correct Address The FDCPA, 15 U.S.C. 1692g ( a ), requires that a debt collector send a written validation notice to the consumers last known address within five days of the initial communication. Your failure to ensure that I received the notice, especially after receiving a returned mail response, does not absolve NRA Group , LLC. of responsibility. Your reliance on incorrect or outdated contact information without further attempts to verify may also constitute a violation of the FDCPA. 
4. Original Creditors Obligation to Maintain Accurate Information If this debt were mine, the original creditor would have had updated and accurate information about my address and contact details. Creditors are obligated under various laws, including the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ), 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( a ), to maintain accurate records and report truthful information. You acknowledge receiving my STOP text response but continued your communication efforts. Any attempts to collect the debt beyond this point should have been in writing and for the limited purposes permitted under the law, such as providing notice of legal action or updating the status of the debt. Sending a text message after receiving the STOP request may have violated this section. 
7. Failure to Update My Credit Report to Reflect " Disputed by Consumer '' Status The Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ), 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( b ), requires that once a debt is disputed, the debt collector must inform the credit reporting agencies that the account is disputed. To date, my credit report has not been updated to reflect the dispute, which is a violation of the FCRA. NRA Group , LLC. has a legal obligation to notify the credit bureaus that the debt is disputed as soon as they are aware of the dispute, regardless of whether the debt has been verified or not. Failure to do so can result in inaccurate reporting, which violates my rights under the FCRA.

a. c. I had to reapply 13 times as during the delay I became XXXX. The banks agent informed me that if there is an application in process they can not proceed with foreclosure. 
d. During the evaluation process a foreclosure was published in the Supreme Court of the State of New York County of XXXX. I was served foreclosure papers in XXXX of XXXX. According to a foreclosure attorney there have been several stages of foreclosure processed on my behalf. 
3. XX/XX/XXXX I was served foreclosure papers by the court however, advised again that if I continue to apply the foreclosure could not go through. I kept reapplying. 
4. XX/XX/XXXX my application was finally accepted however not the extension of the previous coverage but a new forbearance coverage with new terms : a. The pay-off time was changed from 30 years to 40 with a 3-month probation period. 
b. A payment from the XXXX XXXX came through during the probation period, after my first payment and the balance of my debt was paid to the bank. 
c. Without consideration or discussion, the bank canceled my forbearance agreement after my first payment. The new monthly payments have increased.

Finally, there are multiple complaints identifying this behavior as typical from this financial institution to the CFPB and other such institutions. I am not convinced that a technical glitch in a corporation can last as long as they claimed, neither should I have had to apply multiple times for forbearance relief. It is a known fact that this institution does not intend to keep properties in New York as they told me so themselves when attempting to refinance prior to Covid. It appears that they intend to acquire the property, gain the equity and collect an abondance of fees from their clients. 
During this topsy turvy process, I had to care for XXXX household family members who suffered XXXX. There has been mental and physical anguish in the consideration of whether they would have a home to heal in or come home to. I struggled through this process alone trying to figure out how to come up with the money, keep house with no finances and looking for employment while caring for XXXX individuals. I too have now suffered my own maladies due to the stress. This process has taken a detrimental toll on my family, finances and health. Spring Oaks Capital LLC Address : XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX, VA XXXX Debt amount listed on consumer report : {$640.00} Date Opened : XX/XX/XXXX I have received a communication from Spring Oaks Capital LLC regarding an alleged debt. I believe this debt is not mine and the collection agencies have failed to follow appropriate legal and accounting standards in attempting to collect it. Specifically, I contend the following : Lack of Verification and Validation : The collection agency has not provided a copy of the original contract or agreement bearing my wet signature. I request the purchase order agreement from the original creditor. Under 12 CFR 1006.34 ( b ) ( 5 ) and 12 CFR 1006.34 ( c ) ( 4 ) ( i ), I am entitled to verification of the debt, including the name and address of the original creditor and documentation of the debt 's legitimacy. 

Violation of GAAP : The collection agency has not provided any verifiable financial information that adheres to Generally Accepted Accounting Principles ( GAAP ). Without proper documentation, their claims are not substantiated and fail to meet ethical accounting standards. 

Right to Face My Accuser : I am entitled to face my accuser. The debt collector has not provided any evidence that I was informed of the debt being sold, nor was I present during any related transactions. This lack of transparency violates my rights and raises serious concerns about the legitimacy of the debt. 

Unauthorized Reporting : The collection agency has no authority to furnish this alleged account to any consumer reporting agency without proper verification. The false reporting of this debt constitutes defamation of character. 

12 CFR 1006.34 ( b ) ( 5 ) : This regulation requires debt collectors to provide specific information regarding the debt, including the name and address of the original creditor.

12 CFR 1006.34 ( c ) ( 4 ) ( i ) : This regulation mandates that debt collectors provide a detailed statement of the debt, including documentation that supports their claim. 

Provision of Documentation : Provision of the original contract or agreement bearing my wet signature. If such documentation can not be provided, the debt claim should be considered invalid.

It has come to my attention that certain accounts listed on my credit report do not belong to me, and their inclusion is not only inaccurate but also violates my rights as a consumer. Allow me to elaborate on the specific issues I have identified and the laws that support my claim : **15 U.S Code 1681a ( 4 ) - Consumer Right to Privacy : ** The presence of fraudulent accounts on my credit report constitutes an intrusion into my privacy rights. I firmly believe that I have the sole authority to determine what information is private and should be shared on my credit report. 

**FDCPA 807 - Misleading False Reporting : ** The information being reported falsely suggests that I have applied for numerous inquiries and accounts, which is simply not the case. This misleading representation can have detrimental effects on my financial standing and is a violation of the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ).

**15 USC 1681n - Civil Liability for Willful Noncompliance : ** Your agency 's failure to verify the accuracy of credit information before reporting it may result in civil liability. It is imperative that accurate and verified information is reported to ensure fairness and transparency in the credit reporting process.

**18 U.S. Code 1028A - Aggravated Identity Theft : ** Sharing my personal information with creditors without obtaining my consent may constitute aggravated identity theft, a serious criminal offense punishable by law.

**15 U.S. Code 6802 ( b ) 1 ( ) ( a ) ( A ) ( B ) ( C ) - Obligations with Respect to Disclosures of Personal Information : ** Your agency 's failure to disclose my right to opt out of information sharing is concerning and deceptive. As a consumer, I should have the option to exercise my right to privacy and confidentiality regarding my personal information.

**FDCPA 8012 - Furnishing Deceptive Forms : ** Reporting unvalidated debts without proper verification is misleading and deceptive. It is essential that accurate and verified information is reported to avoid any misrepresentation of my financial status.

**15 U.S. Code 1692f - Unfair Practices : ** Reporting unvalidated debts as if they were accurate constitutes an unfair practice. It is essential that all reported information is verified and validated to ensure fairness and accuracy.

**15 U.S. Code 1602 - Definitions and Rules of Construction : ** As the original creditor, I did not grant authorization for the deferral of payments. Your agency 's reporting of inaccurate information violates my rights and undermines the integrity of the credit reporting process.

**FDCPA 806 - Harassment and Abuse : ** Your agency 's actions have caused me undue distress and inconvenience. Despite my efforts to rectify the situation, inaccurate information continues to be reported without my consent, leading to ongoing harassment from creditors.

**Section 1581a ( 3 ) - Identity Theft : ** The illegal acquisition of my personal information and its unauthorized use by creditors constitutes identity theft, a serious offense that must be addressed.

**15 U.S. Code 1692b ( 2 ) - Acquisition of Location Information : ** Reporting debts without my consent is a clear violation of my rights and further compounds the inaccuracies present in my credit report.

**15 U.S. Code 1666b - Timing of Payments : ** Reporting " late payments '' without a clear definition is both inaccurate and deceptive. It is crucial that accurate information is reported to ensure fairness and transparency in the credit reporting process.

**15 U.S. Code 1605 - Determination of Finance Charge : ** Inclusion of inaccurate finance charges further exacerbates the inaccuracies present in my credit report and must be rectified immediately.

**15 U.S. Code 1692d ( 1 ) - Harassment and Abuse : ** Reporting unvalidated debts negatively impacts my reputation and constitutes harassment and abuse. It is imperative that all reported information is accurate and verified to avoid any misrepresentation of my financial status.

**15 U.S. Code 1692j - Furnishing Certain Deceptive Forms : ** Any contracts signed without my authorization constitute a violation of this statute and must be addressed accordingly.

**15 USC 1692h - Multiple Debts : ** Any payments made on unvalidated debts must be returned to me promptly, as per this statute.

**15 U.S. Code 1692g - Validation of Debts : ** Only I can validate debts, and your agency 's failure to remove unvalidated accounts is a violation of my rights as a consumer.

**15 U.S. Code 1681b - Permissible Purposes of Consumer Reports : ** Reporting information without obtaining written consent violates this statute and undermines the integrity of the credit reporting process.

**15 USC 1681i Procedure in case of disputed accuracy : ** Under this law, when a consumer notifies a furnisher that they believe there is inaccurate information on their credit report, the furnisher is required to conduct a reasonable investigation into the dispute. This investigation typically involves reviewing the relevant information provided by the consumer, as well as any supporting documentation, and then either verifying, correcting, or deleting the disputed information as necessary.

The furnisher must complete the investigation within a reasonable timeframe, generally within 30 days, although extensions may be granted under certain circumstances. Once the investigation is complete, the furnisher must report the results back to the consumer and, if applicable, update the information with the CRAs.

Failure to comply with the requirements of **15 U.S. Code 1681i** can result in penalties for the furnisher, including fines and potential legal action by the consumer.

Overall, this law ensures that consumers have the right to challenge and correct inaccurate information on their credit reports, helping to maintain the integrity and fairness of the credit reporting system.

Consumer complaint narrative:
Dear CFPB, I am submitting a formal complaint against Equifax for willfully violating 15 U.S. Code 1681i - Compliance procedures by failing to conduct a reasonable investigation and 15 U.S. Code 1681e ( b ) - Accuracy of report for failing to assure maximum possible accuracy.

I believe the evidence provided substantiates that not only was Equifax in violation of 15 U.S. Code 168o ( a ) ( 1 ) - ( 2 ) for being negligent and non-compliant in their handling this claim, but also violated 15 U.S. Code 1681n ( a ), as they clearly demonstrated willful recklessness throughout the process. This is my final attempt to request that Equifax resolve this matter, or I have no choice but to exercise my private right of action. 

Overview : I mailed Equifax a dispute letter via certified mail on XX/XX/XXXX, and provided 60 pages of evidence, including receipts and official documentation, asking them to investigate inaccurate information reporting on my credit file regarding an erroneous debt of {$4700.00} furnished by DFAS. ( see Exhibit I : Equifax Certified Mail Dispute XXXX ) My letter explained that not only was this debt a mistake on the part of DFAS ( with irrefutable evidence to back it up ), but in addition, I pointed out multiple other errors associated with this account which were reporting inaccurately ( causing adverse action ), and asked Equifax to investigate the errors and to correct the inaccuracies or delete the account. 

As youll find in Exhibit I, I provided Equifax a detailed overview of why the account is inaccurate and started by explaining that I had already contacted DFAS directly regarding the account back in XX/XX/XXXX, and they still hadnt responded to my dispute, so I was asking for Equifax to please investigate the matter directly.

I also explained that I had never received any letters or notices from DFAS regarding this debt. Instead, I discovered it while reviewing my credit report. To this day, DFAS has still not sent me any letters or correspondence regarding the reason for this alleged debt. I explained that I discovered the debt while randomly reviewing my credit report and saw that it was reporting. I explained that after reaching out to multiple departments within DFAS, I finally spoke with a representative named XXXX XXXX on XX/XX/XXXX, who said her ID Number was 24. She was able to pull up the alleged debt and said it was regarding an overpayment due to the weight of a military  household goods move from XXXX XXXX XXXX, in XX/XX/XXXX and that DFAS sent the notice of indebtedness letter to that invalid address in XXXX XXXX XXXX. 

I explained to Equifax that this was clearly a mistake by DFAS because I was NOT in the military in XXXX, nor did I live in XXXX  or have any association with that address in XXXX. I explained that XXXX is a one-party consent state and that I recorded the entire call with DFAS. During this call, I had the DFAS representative, XXXX XXXX, admit that the call was being recorded on her end as well ; however, when I told her the conversation was also being recorded on my end, she put me on hold and then abruptly hung up. Youll find a transcribed copy of this phone call with DFAS later in Exhibit IV. I then pointed out specific evidence to Equifax, which I included within the 60 pages of attachments, and explained there is no possible way this alleged debt could be accurate for the following reasons : 1. The XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX documents I included, validate that I was medically separated from the military in XX/XX/XXXX, NOT in XX/XX/XXXX, and I was located in XXXX XXXX NOT in XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX 

2. I also included all the documents from the military pertaining to my household goods move from when I separated in XX/XX/XXXX ( to include all the receipts from that move that were returned by mail ), clearly indicating that I relocated from XXXX XXXX  to my home of record address in XXXX XXXX. Additionally, I pointed out that block 19a of my XXXX specifically lists my XXXX  mailing address ( Mailing Address After XXXX ) as the Home of Record Address in XXXXXXXX XXXX, and Block XXXX9b ( Nearest Relative ) has the same address. 

After pointing out this evidence, I asked Equifax how it would be possible for me to owe money for an alleged military households good move that took place two years and seven months after I had already XXXX  from the military, from an address in a state where, according to their own records, they I knew didnt live? I also asked them, why would DFAS mail the notice to an address that I am not associated with, in a state they know I dont live in, when according to their own records, they have my mailing address documented as the Home of Record Address in XXXX XXXX XXXX ? Not only does this clearly indicate that the debt DFAS is alleging I owe not valid, but its down right not even possible. Therefor I asked Equifax to please delete the account.

Although this shouldve been more than enough to substantiate my dispute, I proceeded with pointing out several additional errors regarding this account, asking Equifax to investigate and correct the following incomplete or inaccurate information : If this was for an alleged charge in XX/XX/XXXX, then why does the Date Opened say XX/XX/XXXX? Wouldnt this be considered illegally re-aging the debt? 
Why does the date open say XX/XX/XXXX, and Delinquency First Reported say XX/XX/XXXX, but the payment history data on the bottom doesnt have anything listed for XXXX, XXXX, or XX/XX/XXXX? 
Why does this account have a C listed for XXXX and XX/XX/XXXX, indicating its in collections, and why does the account status ( under the summary section ) say COLLECTION, but this account is listed under the Revolving Accounts section of my credit report, and the Account Type says INSTALLMENT? 
Why does it say the Date of First Delinquency is XX/XX/XXXX, but the payment history data on the bottom is blank for XX/XX/XXXX? 
Why is the Actual Payment Amount section blank?

Why is the Date of Last Activity blank?

Why is the Activity Designator blank?

Why is the Creditor Classification UNKNOWN?

Why is the Date Closed blank?

I did my due diligence and spent a lot of time and effort to ensure I provided Equifax with all the evidence they could possibly need to conduct a reasonable investigation. I took the time to ensure everything was organized and presented so that any layperson investigating could look at the evidence and quickly determine this account was not only full of errors but that the debt itself was not valid and needed to be deleted. I then spent over {$40.00} on a mailing service to ensure Equifax properly received all 60 pages in a neat and organized manner via certified mail.

Response From Equifax : On XXXX XXXX XXXX, I received a letter in the mail from Equifax dated XX/XX/XXXX. The letter stated the following : We have received your request concerning inaccurate information on your Equifax credit file. Because the information you provided as proof of your identity does not match the information, we currently have on your credit file, we ask that you send us a copy of two different items- one from each of the two categories listed below. One item will verify your identity and the other will verify your current address ( see Exhibit II : Equifax Stall Letter for ID XXXX ) Knowing that the proof of identity I provided on XX/XX/XXXX, via certified mail DID match the information on my Equifax credit file and that this was nothing more than an unethical stall tactic that Equifax regularly uses to deter consumers from pursuing their legal right to correct inaccurate information on their credit file, I decided to call Equifax at the XXXX number they provided on the letter. I recorded the phone call, including Equifax 's permission, stating, " All calls may be recorded. '' I also had that recording transcribed and attached it here for your review. ( see Exhibit III : Equifax Recording Transcription XXXX ) I waited on hold for over 49 minutes to speak to a representative, which any reasonable person would agree is another deceptive attempt by Equifax to deter consumers from following through with their dispute. During the wait on hold, the automated message gave me the option to listen to the results of my dispute ( see Exhibit III, page 2, timestamp XXXX ) and stated Your dispute was completed on XX/XX/XXXX. The results of your dispute are as follows : for item one. We verified that this item belongs to you. For item two, Additional information has been provided from the original source regarding this item. For item three undefined.

My conversation with the Equifax Dispute Department Representative, XXXX, started approximately 49 minutes into the call. I explained to her the reason why I was calling and pressed her on two main questions. 1. How did Equifax reasonably determine that this account was verified as accurate when I provided an abundance of evidence that clearly proved otherwise? 2. Why did Equifax mail me a letter stating the proof of identity I provided didnt match the information on my credit file when it clearly matched the data on my Equifax Credit File ( Report Confirmation XXXX ) dated XX/XX/XXXX, exactly? ( See Exhibit IV : Equifax Credit File XXXX ) Despite all the evidence I provided, XXXX stated that all Equifax did was forward my dispute to DFAS and then marked it as verified because DFAS said it was. Equifax failed to conduct any independent investigation even though I explicitly stated in my letter that the reason I was disputing through Equifax was that I had already disputed with DFAS directly in XX/XX/XXXX, and they didn't rectify the situation. I even provided Equifax with copies of that dispute with DFAS, which were attached to the 60 pages of evidence I offered them on XX/XX/XXXX via certified mail, which you can find in Exhibit I. Instead of conducting a reasonable investigation, Equifax merely parroted the information that DFAS provided and ignored all my evidence with reckless disregard. 

Notice of Discrepancy in Address ( 15 U.S.C. 1681c ( h ) ) As for XXXX response to the erroneous letter claiming my identity didnt match, refer to Exhibit III, pages 9 - 11, starting at time stamp XXXX to XXXX. She told me to ignore that letter from Equifax because the information I provided was in fact accurate. However, the concern is why she states it was flagged, which would also violate the FCRA. She said this sometimes happens when banks or creditors access my report and provide updates with outdated or inaccurate information, such as an old address unless I request to have that address removed from my file. This is interesting because the address where DFAS allegedly mailed the notice of this erroneous debt was a very old, inaccurate XXXX XXXX XXXX, address that I had already disputed and deleted from my Equifax, XXXX, and XXXX credit files long before this account was ever reported. ( See Exhibit V : DFAS Recorded Call Transcript XXXX ). Youll also see that XXXX, who happens to be another Credit Reporting Agency that furnishes information to the larger CRAs ( such as Equifax ), sent me a random letter dated XX/XX/XXXX, stating they updated that same inaccurate XXXX XXXXXXXX XXXX address on my credit file, even though I had an active security freeze on my XXXX file, which they acknowledged in that same letter. ( See Exhibit VI : XXXX Certified Mail Dispute XXXX ) At that point, the Equifax Representative, XXXX, told me she would process another dispute to reinvestigate the DFAS account. I asked her to mail me a copy of my Complete File Disclosure and made it clear that I was not requesting just a credit report but a Complete File Disclosure, which she acknowledged and repeated back to me. This can be found in Exhibit III. She then gave me a confirmation number of XXXX for the Request for my File Disclosure and XXXX for the Request for Reinvestigation. 

About a week later, I received the Results of the Reinvestigation, dated XX/XX/XXXX, less than two business days from when the representative submitted the request for reinvestigation ( See Exhibit VII. Equifax Reinvestigation Results XXXX ). Once again, Equifax inaccurately claimed that the account was verified. I believe it's important to mention that courts have ruled that Credit Reporting Agencies are required to do more than merely make a cursory investigation to verify disputed information and relying solely on automatic dispute systems, such as the XXXX, to verify an account is accurate, while ignoring evidence provided by the consumer is considered willful.

I also received the response for my File Disclosure, which Im entitled under 15 U.S.C. 1681g, but instead, all Equifax provided was nothing more than a basic credit report, not the Full File Disclosure as requested. ( See Exhibit VIII. Equifax Response for Full File Disclosure XXXX ) It's also worth pointing out that I submitted the same dispute to XXXX, and they DELETED the account right away. ( See Enclosure IX : XXXX  DFAS Account Removed ). How is it possible that when XXXX conducted a reasonable investigation, they determined the account was inaccurate? However, Equifax claims to have reinvestigated the same account twice and " verified it was accurate '' each time. Shouldn't they follow the same industry standard when investigating disputes for incomplete or inaccurate information? 

According to my most recent Equifax Credit File ( Report Confirmation XXXX ), pulled on XX/XX/XXXX, these inaccuracies are still reporting ( See Exhibit X. XXXX Equifax DFAS Reporting XXXX ). As you can see, Equifax is still reporting a Date Open of XX/XX/XXXX, and fails to provide a Date of Last Activity, indicating the account has been illegally re-aged, despite all the evidence Ive provided. The Account Status is reporting as a Collection, and under Comment 1, Comment 2, and Comment 3, it states this is a collection account for XXXX, XXXX, and XXXX ; however, its listed on my report as an Installment Account. As you can clearly see, the Collections section of my credit file states, You currently do not have any Collections in your file. How is that possible? Also, the Balance and the Amount Past Due both report {$4700.00}, which is higher than the High Credit, which reports {$4600.00}. How can the Balance or the past due be higher than the high credit? In addition to that, the Creditor Classification, Activity Designator, Date of Last Activity, Actual Payment Amount, Charge Off Amount, and Terms Frequency are all either blank or unknown.

Consumer complaint narrative:
Dear Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, I am writing to request your assistance in resolving an ongoing issue with Experian regarding the correction and updating of my credit profile. 

On three separate occasions, I sent certified returned receipt letters to Experian requesting updates to my credit profile with the correct information. Each of these requests included three forms of proof of my identity : my ID, my social security card, and proof of address. Despite providing all the necessary documentation, Experian has repeatedly denied my right to correct or update my credit profile. 

Below is an example of Experian 's response to my request : -- - **XXXX XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXX ** " We received a recent request regarding your credit information that does not appear to have been sent directly by you or to be authorized by you. As a precautionary measure, we have not taken any action on your alleged request. According to the federal Fair Credit Reporting Act, 'if the completeness or accuracy of any item of information contained in a consumer 's file at a national consumer credit reporting company is disputed by the consumer and the consumer notifies the company directly of such dispute, the company shall reinvestigate free of charge. ' Therefore, you can dispute any inaccurate information directly with Experian for free. 

If you believe that information in your personal credit report is inaccurate or incomplete, please call us at the phone number XXXX, or visit our secure website to upload your documents at www.experian.com/dispute. '' -- - Despite following their instructions and providing all required documents, my requests have been consistently denied. My most recent attempt to fix my report was on XX/XX/2024, yet I still have not received a satisfactory resolution. I am now seeking the involvement of the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau ( CFPB ) to ensure that this matter is resolved appropriately and to prevent any further unnecessary trauma. 

The Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ) is the U.S. federal law that promotes the accuracy, fairness, and privacy of consumer information contained in the files of consumer reporting agencies. Specifically, under the FCRA, consumers have the right to dispute inaccurate or incomplete information in their credit reports, and the credit bureaus are required to investigate and correct any errors. 

The relevant section of the FCRA that addresses a consumer 's right to dispute and request updates to their credit profile is **Section 611**. This section is codified at **15 U.S.C . 1681i** and details the procedures for disputing the accuracy of information in a consumer 's file.

Key points of Section 611 ( 15 U.S.C. 1681i ) include : 1. **Reinvestigation of Disputed Information** : When a consumer disputes the accuracy of any item of information contained in their credit report, the credit reporting agency ( CRA ) must reinvestigate free of charge and record the current status of the disputed information within 30 days, unless the CRA reasonably determines that the dispute is frivolous or irrelevant.

2. **Prompt Notice of Dispute** : The CRA must promptly notify the furnisher of the information ( such as a creditor ) of the dispute. 

3. **Correction of Errors** : If the information is found to be inaccurate or incomplete or can not be verified, the CRA must promptly delete or modify the item of information.

4. **Notification to the Consumer** : The CRA must provide the consumer with the results of the reinvestigation, a revised credit report if changes were made, and information on their right to add a statement disputing the information if the reinvestigation does not resolve the dispute. 

By utilizing these provisions, consumers can ensure that their credit reports are accurate and up-to-date. It is imperative that Experian adheres to these legal requirements to protect the rights of consumers. 

Furthermore, given that I have sent my ID, social security card, and pay stub, it is unclear how Experian could conclude that I was not sending my own request. This appears to be a stalling tactic that is both frustrating and unwarranted. 

Thank you for your attention to this urgent matter.
